events.what: Butbaia, Vipulanandan, Tan, Huang, Saunders-A'Court, Fagan, Passaro, Tarquini and Gukov report new record lower bounds for the maximal {+1,-1} determinant at orders 51, 107, 111, 115 and 119, with explicit matrices in a companion repository
events.ai_basis: The findings presented in this work grew out of research conducted at the Caltech Math–AI Lab, whose mission is to develop new AI systems and algorithms capable of performing effectively in sparse–reward, long-horizon environments.

events.what: Maximal determinants of matrices over the l-th roots of unity

judgement.doubts: The AI role is the real question. The paper's own quoted sentence only says the work 'grew out of research' at an AI lab, which is the F9 thin-quote example verbatim and does not say a model produced the matrices. The record says the lab's website credits this result to 'RL-based solvers', but the researcher could not read the paper's methods section. If the paper or repository states that an RL system found the matrices, the right code is 'generated' (or 'assisted' if people refined the output). The status 'progress' is correct: record entries at five orders are bounds, and the true maxima there are still unknown.

corrections.why: F9: 'bound' is not a valid AI-role value, and the only quote from the paper ('grew out of research conducted at the Caltech Math–AI Lab') does not say what any AI system produced. That is the thin-quote case. The record's own competing_reading notes the paper body never describes an RL algorithm, and the RL credit comes from the lab's website, not the paper. Coded on what the quote supports and flagged: upgrade to 'generated' or 'assisted' if the methods section confirms an RL system found the matrices.

F3: kept. New record determinants at orders 51, 107, 111, 115 and 119 are lower bounds (per the record, 'the true maximum at those orders is still unknown'), not a determination of any value, so this is progress, not partial or resolved.
